## Draft — display only (not executed here)
Rev code is for reading / pasting into RevBayes (it does not run as a Quarto cell), and
**has not been executed in this repo**. The authoritative, maintained versions are
Rosana Zenil-Ferguson's **[BiSSE and HiSSE tutorials](https://roszenil.github.io/mytutorials/contenido.html)**
and the RevBayes **[state-dependent diversification tutorials](https://revbayes.github.io/tutorials/#diversification-rate-estimation)**.
See [`SETUP.md`](SETUP.md) for install + data. Use those pages for the exact dataset/scripts;
below is a teaching skeleton with a generic **binary plant trait** (e.g. woody = 0 /
herbaceous = 1).
:::

## Goal

Ask whether a **binary trait** affects speciation/extinction — and then confront the
**false-positive problem** from the [diversification lecture](../06-diversification.qmd) by
comparing **BiSSE** to a **hidden-state (HiSSE) / character-independent (CID)** null.

## 1. Setup and data

```{.rev}
NUM_STATES = 2
observed_phylogeny = readTrees("data/plant_tree.tre")[1]
data = readCharacterDataDelimited("data/plant_trait.tsv",
        stateLabels=2, type="NaturalNumbers", delimiter="\t", headers=FALSE)

taxa = observed_phylogeny.taxa()
root_age <- observed_phylogeny.rootAge()
rho <- 250 / 300              # sampling fraction: sampled / described species

moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()
```

## 2. Speciation & extinction per state

```{.rev}
# a shared mean, exponential priors; one rate per observed state
rate_mean <- ln( taxa.size() ) / root_age    # rough expected net-diversification scale

for (i in 1:NUM_STATES) {
    speciation[i] ~ dnExponential(1.0 / rate_mean)
    extinction[i] ~ dnExponential(1.0 / rate_mean)
    moves.append( mvScale(speciation[i], weight=2) )
    moves.append( mvScale(extinction[i], weight=2) )
}
```

## 3. Trait transition rates (the Q matrix)

```{.rev}
# anagenetic transitions between states 0 and 1
rate_pr := observed_phylogeny.treeLength() / 10
q01 ~ dnExponential(rate_pr)
q10 ~ dnExponential(rate_pr)
moves.append( mvScale(q01, weight=2) )
moves.append( mvScale(q10, weight=2) )

rate_matrix := fnFreeK( [q01, q10], rescaled=false )

# equal prior on the root state
root_freq <- simplex( rep(1, NUM_STATES) )
```

## 4. The character-dependent birth–death process

```{.rev}
bisse ~ dnCDBDP( rootAge          = root_age,
                 speciationRates  = speciation,
                 extinctionRates  = extinction,
                 Q                = rate_matrix,
                 pi               = root_freq,
                 rho              = rho,
                 condition        = "survival" )

bisse.clamp( observed_phylogeny )
bisse.clampCharData( data )
```

## 5. MCMC + ancestral states

```{.rev}
mymodel = model(bisse)

monitors.append( mnModel(filename="output/bisse.log", printgen=10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(printgen=100, speciation, extinction) )
monitors.append( mnJointConditionalAncestralState(
        tree=observed_phylogeny, cdbdp=bisse, type="NaturalNumbers",
        printgen=10, withTips=true, withStartStates=false,
        filename="output/bisse_anc.log") )

mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, moves, monitors)
mymcmc.run(generations=20000)   # check ESS in Tracer; real runs are longer

anc = readAncestralStateTrace("output/bisse_anc.log")
ancestralStateTree(observed_phylogeny, anc, "output/bisse_anc.tre",
                   state_labels=["0","1"])
```

## 6. Visualize (R + RevGadgets)

```{.r}
library(RevGadgets)
# posterior speciation rates by state
trace <- readTrace("output/bisse.log")
plotTrace(trace, vars = c("speciation[1]", "speciation[2]"))[[1]]

# ancestral states painted on the tree
anc <- processAncStates("output/bisse_anc.tre",
                        state_labels = c("0" = "woody", "1" = "herbaceous"))
plotAncStatesMAP(anc, tree_layout = "rectangular")
```

::: {.figure-prompt}
**FIGURE (student output)** — (a) posterior densities of $\lambda_0$ vs $\lambda_1$
(overlap ⟹ no trait effect); (b) ancestral states on the tree.
:::

## 7. The catch — is it real? HiSSE / CID null

BiSSE will happily report $\lambda_0 \neq \lambda_1$ even when the true driver is a **hidden**
factor (lecture: Rabosky & Goldberg 2015). Refit with a hidden state and a
**character-independent (CID)** null, then compare by **marginal likelihood** (Bayes factor).

```{.rev}
# HiSSE sketch: expand to NUM_STATES x NUM_HIDDEN classes
NUM_HIDDEN = 2
NUM_TOTAL  = NUM_STATES * NUM_HIDDEN
# speciation/extinction now vary by hidden class; observed trait may (HiSSE)
# or may NOT (CID null) modulate the rates. Build the combined Q with
# fnCombineHiddenStates()-style construction and rerun dnCDBDP over NUM_TOTAL states.
```

- **HiSSE fits better than BiSSE** ⟹ diversification varies, but not (only) with your trait.
- **CID null fits as well as HiSSE** ⟹ rate heterogeneity is **unrelated** to the trait —
  do **not** claim the trait drives diversification.

::: {.callout-tip}
Report the model comparison, not just the BiSSE rate difference. A significant BiSSE result
that collapses under a CID null is the single most common SSE mistake.
:::

## The lesson

- **BiSSE** estimates per-state $\lambda,\mu$ + trait transitions and paints ancestral states.
- A raw BiSSE "signal" is **not** evidence of causation — one radiating clade can create it.
- Always fit **HiSSE + a CID null** and compare. For plants, apply this to selfing, ploidy,
  or growth form (link to popgen decks 03/06).
